content.snl: def-hyp(list-partial(Type.judge(@F, Analysis.PFun), Type.judge(list-partial(@a, @b), Real), $#0 < #1$(a, b)), Analysis.contOnIcc(F, a, b), Logic.and(Analysis.contOn(F, Ioo(a, b)), Logic.and(Analysis.contRightAt(F, a), Analysis.contLeftAt(F, b))))
content.markdown:
Continuity on `[a, b]` means continuity on the open interior together with right-continuity at `a` and left-continuity at `b`. Demanding two-sided continuity at the endpoints would be wrong: it would force `F` to be defined outside `[a, b]`, so no function with domain exactly `[a, b]` could ever satisfy it.

The convention presupposes `a < b`; it is the hypothesis under which the closed-interval theorems below are stated.
